t:
(a) 
Subject to the provisions of section 1508 of the Revised Statutes, all promotions to grades above that of lieutenant (junior grade), including the promotion of those officers who are, or may be, carried on the Navy list as additional numbers in grade, shall be only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as herein prescribed.
 
    (b) 
Rear admirals, not restricted in the performance of duty, who complete four years of service in that grade and thirty-four years of total commissioned service shall, subject to the provisions of subsection 107 (a) of this title, be continued on the active list only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as prescribed by titles I through IV of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "board" making recommendations before a federal decision is like an advisory committee. That fails because the board is made up entirely of naval officers, who are federal personnel, so the promotion and retention process stays inside the federal government. No outside party such as the public, states, or outside experts is consulted or given a right to object or sue.
fable.s: shall be only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as herein prescribed

qwen_block.w: The section requires that promotions be based on the recommendation of a 'board of naval officers.' Naval officers are federal employees and thus inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination between federal officials or employees is not participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or non-federal experts.
qwen_block.s: all promotions to grades above that of lieutenant (junior grade)... shall be only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as herein prescribed.

opus.w: The only body that takes part in the promotion and retention decisions is a board of naval officers. Its members are federal military personnel doing their official jobs, so everyone involved is inside the federal government. The board-recommendation language looks like an advisory committee, but no states, experts, members of the public or other outside parties are involved, so this is not participation under the definition.
opus.s: shall be only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as herein prescribed.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that promotions "only upon the recommendation of a board" sound like an advisory body shaping a federal decision. That fails here because the board is made up entirely of naval officers, who are federal personnel.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires recommendations from a board of naval officers for promotions. Naval officers are federal employees, which places them inside the federal government. The definition of participation requires consultation or coordination with people OUTSIDE the federal government (e.g., states, public, experts). Internal military boards composed of service members do not constitute outside participation.
qwen_chat.s: all promotions to grades above that of lieutenant (junior grade)... shall be only upon the recommendation of a board of naval officers as herein prescribed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that a "board of naval officers" constitutes an advisory body whose recommendations are required before a decision (promotion) is made, thus fitting the definition of participation. However, the definition explicitly states that federal officials and employees are INSIDE the federal government. Since naval officers are federal employees, their internal deliberations and recommendations are intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
